title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.01879699248; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. The preregistered primary hypothesis test was the exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired verifier outcomes (decision rule α = 0.05); the paired bootstrap (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593985, 0.0375939850] is reported as a supplementary descriptive interval, not as a replacement for the preregistered decision rule. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded and thus the preregistered latency estimand could not be evaluated. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We archive exact paired counts, provider/stage accounting, representative validator and repair traces, and contamination findings to support reproducibility and audit.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1]. Stochastic LLM outputs can produce syntactic or semantic violations—missing required commands, unsafe command ordering, or constraint breaches—that create operational risk if applied directly. To mitigate such risks, generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines interpose deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish‑style tools) and bounded repair loops to provide deterministic acceptance criteria and automated correction [3]. Prior work proposes GVR architectures and demonstrates prototype integrations, but preregistered paired evaluations that archive verifier traces and quantify verifier‑triggered repair benefits on reproducible NetOps task banks are limited.

This study asks the preregistered confirmatory question (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1): Does a GVR pipeline that uses a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call reduce deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures relative to the same initial candidate without repair? Our principal contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation executed under the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher constraints that reports exact paired counts, the preregistered decision procedure, execution accounting, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples, and an evidence‑grounded interpretation.
sections.related_work: LLM applications in NetOps cover intent‑to‑configuration translation, configuration generation, and AIOps toolchains; recent benchmark and survey efforts document both promise and failure modes [1,2]. Benchmarks such as NetConfEval study synthesis of vendor CLI fragments from intent descriptions and show that vendor‑specific syntax, sequencing, and implicit ordering constraints remain challenging for unconstrained generation [1]. Surveys and system proposals emphasize grounding, verifier integration, and repair as primary mitigations for hallucination and constraint violations [2,3]. Generate–verify–repair architectures have been advanced in adjacent domains (code generation, regulated documents) to combine stochastic generators with deterministic oracles and bounded repair steps [3]. Network verification tools (e.g., Batfish and header‑space analyses) provide practical acceptance tests for reachability, sequencing, and policy constraints; their coverage limits directly shape the observable benefit of GVR loops [4]. Our study differs by executing a preregistered paired test under shared_initial_candidate semantics, archiving raw validator traces, and reporting exact paired contingency counts and both the preregistered test outcome and a supplementary bootstrap CI.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment followed the preregistered plan cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under these semantics the identical single sampled initial model candidate per task is used to produce both outcomes: (1) baseline — score the single initial candidate with the deterministic validator; (2) guarded — if that same candidate fails the validator, the pipeline may invoke at most one automated LLM repair call and then rescore with the same validator. This design isolates the verifier‑triggered repair effect for a fixed initial draw and matches the preregistered execution contract.

Primary inferential rule (preregistered): The exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired binary verifier outcomes was the preregistered primary hypothesis test and decision procedure (α = 0.05). Interval estimation using a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) was prespecified as a descriptive uncertainty summary; we report it as supplementary and do not use it to overturn the preregistered McNemar decision rule.

Task bank, sampling, and inclusion rules: A deterministic generator produced N=300 intent→CLI pairs stratified into two vendor clusters (150 Cisco‑like, 150 Juniper‑like) per the preregistration. Inclusion/exclusion rules followed the preregistered contract: exact public duplicates flagged by contamination checks would be excluded (none were exact duplicates here). Provider/API transient failures triggered up to two automatic retries; pairs in which both arms failed due to infrastructure/model errors were excluded from the primary paired analysis per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (see Results for counts). All task manifest entries, seeds, and contamination checks are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model orchestration and provider/stage accounting semantics: The declared generation model was recorded as gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The run used shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single model generation (stage label shared_initial_generation) produced the sampled candidate used to evaluate both baseline and guarded outcomes. The 'repair' stage count records additional model calls invoked only when the shared initial candidate failed the validator; repair calls are not independent new initial draws. Provider/stage accounting in the execution manifest therefore should be read as model‑call stage counts (shared_initial_generation = single sampled candidate per pair; repair = extra calls when invoked) rather than as independent per‑condition first‑pass generation counts. The reconciled provider accounting for this run is archived and used to explain repair frequency and call totals.

Deterministic validator and scoring: The binary oracle deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforced an archived rule battery per episode: (1) CLI syntactic parsing/normalization; (2) required‑sequence checks against the task's required_sequence; (3) constrained‑field touch checks against allowed_touched_fields and allowed_fields; and (4) reachability/constraint checks over the deterministic synthetic topology (Batfish‑style). Each episode archives validation_before and validation_after objects with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, normalized_configuration, and a boolean valid flag. The primary binary endpoint used the 'full_intent_constraint_validation' scoring rule (scoring JSONs archived) to produce paired binary outcomes.

Repair loop bounding and prompts: The automated repair stage was strictly bounded to at most one LLM repair call per episode when the initial candidate failed. Repair prompts included the task constraints, validator failure diagnostics, and explicit corrective instructions; all repair prompts, provider traces, and repaired outputs are archived. Stage accounting records repair = 6 repair calls in this run.

Analysis procedures: The preregistered primary test was the exact two‑sided McNemar test on paired verifier outcomes. A paired bootstrap percentile CI (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) for the paired difference was computed as a descriptive interval. Missingness handling in the primary analysis followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule: pairs with both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures were excluded from the confirmatory McNemar test; a preregistered conservative sensitivity analysis treats excluded episodes as failures and is reported in Results. All analysis code, resampling parameters, and artifacts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and sample flow: The preregistered plan targeted 300 independent intent→CLI tasks (600 episodes across two conditions). The run recorded planned_episode_count = 600 and completed_episode_count = 532; provider/infrastructure transient failures produced failed_episode_count = 68. Applying the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' exclusion rules (exclude both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures) yielded complete paired units analysed = 266. Provider accounting recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 306 total model‑call events, with completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272 and failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34; stage accounting recorded shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6. These reconciliation artifacts are archived and permit independent verification of model‑call accounting and stage semantics.

Primary paired outcomes: For the 266 complete pairs the validator outcomes produced the contingency counts: n11 = 260 (both baseline and guarded pass), n10 = 5 (guarded pass only), n01 = 0 (baseline pass only), and n00 = 1 (both fail). Observed per‑condition proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090 and guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015; paired (guarded − baseline) difference = 0.01879699248. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 5, n01 = 0) produced p = 0.0625 (did not meet α = 0.05), and the paired bootstrap percentile CI (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) is [0.0037593985, 0.0375939850] (reported supplementaryly).

Missingness application: In accordance with the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule, 34 both‑arm episodes affected by infrastructure/provider failures were excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis, producing the analysed complete_pairs = 266. This exclusion rule and the reconciled counts are recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifacts archived with the run (deterministic_reconciliation.json in the evidence bundle). A conservative sensitivity analysis treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333; the discordant pattern among analysed pairs remains n10 = 5, n01 = 0 and the exact McNemar p remains 0.0625 for the primary paired subset.

Repair invocation and yield: Repair was invoked in 6 episodes. The contingency pattern (n10 = 5) indicates that at most five of those repair invocations converted a failing initial candidate into a guarded pass among analysed pairs; at most one repair among repaired complete pairs did not produce a pass. Median repair iterations per task across analysed pairs is 0. A descriptive number‑needed‑to‑treat (NNT) interpretation on the observed paired difference gives 1 / 0.01879699248 ≈ 53.2 (rough descriptive scalar), reflecting that with a high baseline pass rate the marginal correction yield per repair opportunity is small. Representative per‑episode validator and repair traces (e.g., task-000008) are archived and illustrate typical repair behavior (truncated token corrected; final validation_after.valid = true). These per‑episode artifacts include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation codes, and normalized_configuration and are provided to support targeted audit and diagnostics.

Inference summary: Under the preregistered primary decision rule (exact two‑sided McNemar at α = 0.05), the guarded GVR pipeline did not achieve a formally significant improvement (p = 0.0625). The supplementary paired bootstrap CI excludes zero for the observed sample; because the bootstrap interval is a descriptive estimator specified alongside the preregistered McNemar test, we report it to quantify effect magnitude and sampling variability but do not use it to overturn the preregistered hypothesis test. Key numeric artifacts supporting these summaries (paired contingency table, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and hashed in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation and small‑discordant counts: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (~1.88 percentage points) in verifier pass rate. The preregistered exact McNemar test (two‑sided) did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625) because the discordant pair total is small (n10 + n01 = 5). The paired bootstrap CI (B = 10,000) excludes zero and summarizes resampled paired differences; both inferential perspectives are valid descriptions of sampled uncertainty. We explicitly preserve the preregistered McNemar decision as the formal primary result and provide the bootstrap CI as descriptive context.

Operational implications and boundary conditions: The run’s high baseline first‑pass accuracy (≈97.7%) left few failures for the repair stage to correct, producing infrequent repairs (6/300). Under these conditions the bounded automated repair produced a small marginal benefit and a high descriptive NNT. GVR pipelines will likely yield larger absolute improvements on corpora with lower first‑pass accuracy or when verifier coverage expands to detect additional failure modes. Per‑episode latency—part of the preregistered H2—was not archived and therefore could not be evaluated; we recommend per‑episode timing instrumentation in future runs.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial draw and does not measure independent multiple draws or constrained first‑pass prompting. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule battery; semantic violations outside that battery are undetected. External validity: tasks derive from NetConfEval‑style public items and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor dialects; results may not generalize to other vendors, larger topologies, or production heterogeneity. Conclusion validity: loss of 34 both‑arm provider failures reduced effective N and limited power for small effects.

Design lessons grounded in artifacts: (1) When baseline pass rates are high, evaluate GVR on lower‑baseline corpora or include arms that modify first‑pass sampling (multiple draws or constrained prompts) to increase discordant counts and power. (2) Archive per‑episode pipeline timing to assess latency estimands; our run lacked per‑episode timing. (3) Expand and publish validator rule coverage and include verifier false‑negative tests; per‑episode validator traces permit such audits. (4) Consider separate preregistered arms comparing shared_initial_candidate semantics to independent initial draws when the research question targets first‑pass generation strategies.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that evaluated a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved verifier pass rate by 0.01879699248 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625); a paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) is reported as supplementary and narrowly excludes zero for the observed sample. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be assessed. All execution and analysis artifacts (raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests) are archived in the evidence bundle to support reanalysis and follow‑on work.

Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (preregistration manifest archived). Execution artifacts (raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, deterministic_reconciliation and analysis artifacts) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by the preregistration.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.

Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
